assays.assay_description: 5 min test swim in a plastic cylindrical tank (114 cm × 30.5 cm) with 30 cm water at 28-30 °C, preceded by a 15 min pre-exposure swim. Behaviours scored manually as immobility, swimming, climbing (diving not observed).

application_type.evidence: A single bolus injection... was administered in a volume of 1 mL/kg intraperitoneally (IP)

setup_habituation.evidence: A 15 min preexposure to the paradigm is required to elicit measurable depressive-like behavior

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were placed into a plastic cylindrical tank... could not support themselves by touching the bottom

food_restriction.evidence: Food not present in the FST cylinder during the recording session

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water accessible inside the FST cylinder

time_to_assay.evidence: tested in the FST on days 7, 14, 21, 28, and 35... iPSI pre-exposed on day 34 and tested on day 35; LSD tested on day 35; ketamine groups tested across multiple weeks

sample_size.evidence: SAL (n=8), rPSI (n=8), iPSI (n=8); LSD experiment SAL (n=6), LSD (n=6); ketamine groups (n=6 each); final experiment SAL/KET/PSI (n=6 each)

outcomes.summary: A single i.p. dose of psilocybin (1 mg/kg) or LSD (0.15 mg/kg) significantly reduced immobility and increased swimming (and climbing for psilocybin) in the FST up to 5 weeks post-administration in male WKY rats. Low-dose ketamine (5 mg/kg) reduced immobility at 1 and 2 weeks post-injection but the effect was transient and absent at 3-5 weeks; 20 and 100 mg/kg ketamine had no effect.
outcomes.statistics: rPSI vs SAL: p<0.05 (day 28), p<0.05 (day 35); iPSI vs SAL: immobility p<0.0001, swimming p<0.0001, climbing p<0.0001; LSD vs SAL: immobility p<0.05, swimming p<0.05, climbing p<0.05; KET 5 mg/kg vs SAL: p<0.001 (week 1), p<0.01 (week 2); PSI vs SAL day 7: p<0.0001; PSI vs SAL day 35: p<0.001
outcomes.evidence: Both psilocybin and LSD significantly reduced depressive-like behaviors 5 weeks after administration... 5.0 mg/kg, but not 20 or 100 mg/kg, ketamine significantly reduced immobility in the FST 1 week (p < 0.001) and 2 weeks (p < 0.01) following ketamine administration

assays.assay_description: Square open field arena (61 × 61 cm) with 45 cm opaque walls; rats explored freely for 5 min immediately prior to each FST. Distance traveled (cm) was scored using EthoVision XT 8.5.

application_type.evidence: drugs were administered intraperitoneally (IP) on day 0

setup_habituation.evidence: Paper does not describe a separate pre-test habituation to the open field arena

setup_restrain.evidence: allowing the rats to explore freely for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the open field arena during recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the open field arena during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: LCA was assessed in the open field immediately prior to each FST (days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35)

sample_size.evidence: Same animals as FST experiments; SAL/rPSI/iPSI n=8; LSD/SAL n=6; KET/PSI n=6

outcomes.summary: No differences in overt locomotor activity were observed between psilocybin-, LSD-, or ketamine-treated rats and saline controls at any timepoint, indicating no persistent stimulant or sedative effects.
outcomes.evidence: No differences in overt locomotor activity (LCA) were observed between treatment and control rats (Supplementary Figure S1)

assays.assay_description: Plus-shaped maze with four equally sized arms (two open, two enclosed; arms 50 × 10 cm; maze 114 cm externally). Following ≥15 min room habituation, rats were placed at the central junction facing an open arm and explored freely for 5 min. Time in open arms and closed arms scored with EthoVision 8.5.

application_type.evidence: drugs were administered intraperitoneally (IP) on day 0

setup_habituation.evidence: Each rat was allowed to habituate to the testing room for at least 15 min prior to exposure to the maze (room habituation only, not apparatus habituation)

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to explore freely for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the EPM apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the EPM apparatus during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: Rats were tested for anxiety-like behaviors in the EPM on day 40 (LSD) or day 41 (psilocybin/ketamine experiments)

sample_size.evidence: SAL n=8, rPSI n=7 (one excluded), iPSI n=8; LSD/SAL n=6; PSI/KET/SAL n=6

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin-treated rats that had weekly open-field exposures (rPSI and PSI groups) spent significantly more time in the open arms and less in the closed arms of the EPM than saline controls, indicating an anxiolytic effect. iPSI (psilocybin without weekly arena exposure), LSD, and ketamine did not differ from saline.
outcomes.statistics: rPSI vs SAL: open arms p<0.05, closed arms p<0.05; PSI vs SAL: open arms p<0.05, closed arms p<0.05; iPSI, LSD, KET: not significantly different from SAL
outcomes.evidence: rPSI (n = 7 due to exclusion) spent significantly more time in the open arms of the EPM (p < 0.05) and significantly less time in the closed arms of the EPM (p < 0.05) than SAL (n = 8)... PSI (n = 6) rats spent significantly more time in the open arms (p < 0.05) and significantly less time in the closed arms (p < 0.05) than SAL rats. KET (n = 6) rats were not statistically different from SAL (n = 6) rats.

B1_num_measures.evidence: scored for time spent in the open arms, the closed arms, and the junction

B4_ethological.evidence: Time in zones is a spatial measure, not ethological

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are not scored as shelter per rubric

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are open-ended extensions, scored 0 per rubric

judge_notes: Consolidated three assays: Forced Swim Test, Open Field (locomotor activity), and Elevated Plus Maze, present across all candidates.
Collapsed all drug arms (psilocybin, LSD, ketamine doses; rPSI/iPSI/PSI groupings) into single assay entries per rubric (same paradigm, different manipulations).
B1 for FST set to score 2 (3 measures: immobility, swimming, climbing) following glm/qwen; gptoss undercounted to 2-3 range but assigned score 1.
Set EPM setup_habituation to 'no' because the paper describes only room habituation, which the rubric explicitly excludes from setup_habituation.
day_night_flipped marked not_reported (medium confidence) — paper states 12:12 cycle but does not specify direction or testing phase.
DOI taken from masthead reference (10.1021/acschemneuro.9b00493), agreed by two candidates.
